chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:
"When a man says 'I swore' or 'I took an oath', it is not valid until he says 'I swore by Allah' or 'I took an oath by Allah'.

key_terms.بِاللَّهِ: By Allah (the essential element of the oath)

ai.seo_question: What is required for an oath to be considered valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the technical requirement for the validity of an oath (*yamin*) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between mere verbal intent and the specific invocation of Allah's name. It establishes that general phrases like 'I swear' or 'I took an oath' are legally insufficient unless explicitly coupled with 'by Allah,' ensuring precision in legal obligations and expiations (*kaffarah*). This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on explicit declaration (*zahir*) in personal vows to avoid ambiguity in religious duties.
